/-!
# Albertson conjecture

The *Albertson conjecture* relates the crossing number of a graph to its chromatic number:
among all graphs with chromatic number $n$, the complete graph $K_n$ has the smallest crossing
number. Equivalently, every finite graph $G$ satisfies
$\operatorname{cr}(G) \ge \operatorname{cr}(K_{\chi(G)})$.

The *crossing number* $\operatorname{cr}(G)$ of a finite graph $G$ is the minimum number of edge
crossings over all drawings of $G$ in the plane. A drawing places the vertices at distinct points
and represents each edge by a simple arc between the images of its endpoints which does not pass
through the image of any vertex. A crossing is an unordered pair of distinct edges together with a
point of the plane lying in the interior of both of their arcs. The crossing number is not in
Mathlib, so it is defined here. No genericity conditions ("good drawing") are imposed on
drawings: a crossing-minimal drawing can always be chosen to be good, and every drawing has at
least as many crossings in the above sense as the classical crossing number, so the minimum is
unchanged.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Albertson conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albertson_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [ACF09] M. O. Albertson, D. W. Cranston, J. Fox, *Colorings, crossings, and cliques*,
  Electron. J. Combin. 16 (2009), R45. [arXiv:1006.3783](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.3783)
- [BT10] J. Barát, G. Tóth, *Towards the Albertson conjecture*, Electron. J. Combin. 17 (2010),
  R73. [arXiv:0909.0413](https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.0413)
-/

justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a drawing/embedding of a graph in the plane; the crossing number is a minimum over such drawings. @[category API, AMS 5]
theorem crossingNumber_bot [Countable V] : crossingNumber (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := exists_injective_nat V
  have hbot : ∀ e : (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).edgeSet, False := fun e => by simpa using e.2
  let D : Drawing (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) :=
    { vertex := fun v => EuclideanSpace.single 0 (f v : ℝ)
      vertex_injective := fun v w hvw => by
        have := congrArg (fun p : ℝ² => p 0) hvw
        simpa [EuclideanSpace.single_apply, hf.eq_iff] using this
      arc := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      arc_continuous := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      arc_injective := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      arc_endpoints := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      arc_interior_not_mem_range := fun e => (hbot e).elim }
  rw [crossingNumber, ENat.iInf_eq_zero]
  exact ⟨D, by rw [D.crossings_bot, Set.encard_empty]⟩

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem crossingNumber_mono {H : SimpleGraph V} (hHG : H ≤ G) :
    crossingNumber H ≤ crossingNumber G := by
  let ι : H.edgeSet → G.edgeSet := fun e => ⟨e, SimpleGraph.edgeSet_mono hHG e.2⟩
  have hι : Function.Injective ι := fun e f h => Subtype.ext (congrArg Subtype.val h :)
  refine le_iInf fun D => ?_
  let D' : Drawing H :=
    { vertex := D.vertex
      vertex_injective := D.vertex_injective
      arc := fun e => D.arc (ι e)
      arc_continuous := fun e => D.arc_continuous (ι e)
      arc_injective := fun e => D.arc_injective (ι e)
      arc_endpoints := fun e => D.arc_endpoints (ι e)
      arc_interior_not_mem_range := fun e => D.arc_interior_not_mem_range (ι e) }
  refine (iInf_le _ D').trans ?_
  have hinj : Function.Injective (Prod.map (Sym2.map ι) (id : ℝ² → ℝ²)) :=
    (Sym2.map.injective hι).prodMap Function.injective_id
  rw [← hinj.encard_image]
  refine Set.encard_le_encard ?_
  rintro ⟨p, x⟩ ⟨⟨q, y⟩, ⟨e, f, hef, rfl, hx1, hx2⟩, h⟩
  simp only [Prod.map, id, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
  obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := h
  exact ⟨ι e, ι f, fun h => hef (hι h), by simp, hx1, hx2⟩

claims.decomposer_note: Single universal Prop: for every finite simple graph G, cr(G) ≥ cr(K_{χ(G)}) (equivalently, χ(G) ≥ r ⇒ cr(G) ≥ cr(K_r), as stated by Albertson–Cranston–Fox; the two forms agree since cr(K_r) is monotone in r); the crossing number (minimum number of edge crossings over all drawings in the plane) is not in Mathlib and must be defined; the article's strengthened form (Guy's formula) and weaker Ω(n^4) form are not posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the slot in substance faithfully (cr(K_{χ(G)}) ≤ cr(G) for finite simple graphs, with a bespoke topological crossing number). c03 is the cleanest and most robust: general vertex type with [Finite V], parametrized Jordan arcs on the unit interval into ℝ² with endpoints via Sym2.map and interiors avoiding vertex points, crossings counted as (unordered pair of distinct edges, common interior point) via Set.encard (so overlaps give ⊤, never a spurious 0), ℕ∞-valued ⨅ over drawings (⊤ rather than 0 if no drawing existed), and three proven API lemmas testing the definitions (crossings_bot, crossingNumber_bot, crossingNumber_mono — the last also showing the '=χ(G)' and '≤χ(G)' forms agree). Hypothesis G.chromaticNumber = n is the literal 'same chromatic number' reading and is always satisfiable for finite graphs. Compared with alternatives: c05/c06/c07 use ℕ-valued sInf (rely on sInf ∅ = 0 being unreachable) and clunkier arc encodings (ℝ → ℝ×ℝ with InjOn, Quot.out); c01 restricts to SimpleGraph (Fin n) and uses ncard; c02/c04/c08 are essentially equivalent to c03 (c04/c08 with set-valued arcs) but with less/equal API. Edits to c03: reworded the module docstring (crossing definition, justification of counting convention) and expanded references (added Barát–Tóth, journal data).
claims.source_text: the crossing number can be lower-bounded by the crossing number of a complete graph with the same chromatic number
claims.text_span: the crossing number can be lower-bounded by the crossing number of a complete graph with the same chromatic number

context:
In combinatorial mathematics, the Albertson conjecture is an unproven relationship between the crossing number and the chromatic number of a graph. It is named after Michael O. Albertson, a professor at Smith College, who stated it as a conjecture in 2007; it is one of his many conjectures in graph coloring theory. The conjecture states that, among all graphs requiring $n$ colors, the complete graph $K_{n}$ is the one with the smallest crossing number.
Equivalently, if a graph can be drawn with fewer crossings than $K_{n}$, then, according to the conjecture, it may be colored with fewer than $n$ colors.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition is correct; both suggested forms (equality of chromatic number, or r ≤ χ(G)) are faithful, and the equality form was used to match 'the same chromatic number' verbatim.

/-!
# Albertson conjecture

The *Albertson conjecture* relates the crossing number of a graph to its chromatic number:
among all graphs with chromatic number $n$, the complete graph $K_n$ has the smallest crossing
number. Equivalently, every finite graph $G$ satisfies
$\operatorname{cr}(G) \ge \operatorname{cr}(K_{\chi(G)})$.

The *crossing number* $\operatorname{cr}(G)$ of a finite graph $G$ is the minimum number of edge
crossings over all drawings of $G$ in the plane. A drawing places the vertices at distinct points
and represents each edge by a simple arc between the images of its endpoints which does not pass
through the image of any vertex. A crossing is an unordered pair of distinct edges together with a
point of the plane lying in the interior of both of their arcs. The crossing number is not in
Mathlib, so it is defined here. No genericity conditions ("good drawing") are imposed on
drawings: a crossing-minimal drawing can always be chosen to be good, and every drawing has at
least as many crossings in the above sense as the classical crossing number, so the minimum is
unchanged.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Albertson conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albertson_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [ACF09] M. O. Albertson, D. W. Cranston, J. Fox, *Colorings, crossings, and cliques*,
  Electron. J. Combin. 16 (2009), R45. [arXiv:1006.3783](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.3783)
- [BT10] J. Barát, G. Tóth, *Towards the Albertson conjecture*, Electron. J. Combin. 17 (2010),
  R73. [arXiv:0909.0413](https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.0413)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry unitInterval

namespace AlbertsonConjecture

variable {V : Type*}

/-- A drawing of a simple graph `G` in the plane. The vertices are placed at distinct points,
and each edge is represented by a simple arc (a continuous injective map from the unit interval)
whose endpoints are the images of the two endpoints of the edge and whose interior does not pass
through the image of any vertex. -/
structure Drawing (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  /-- The point of the plane at which a vertex is placed. -/
  vertex : V → ℝ²
  vertex_injective : Function.Injective vertex
  /-- The arc representing an edge. -/
  arc : G.edgeSet → I → ℝ²
  arc_continuous (e : G.edgeSet) : Continuous (arc e)
  arc_injective (e : G.edgeSet) : Function.Injective (arc e)
  /-- The endpoints of the arc of an edge are the images of the endpoints of the edge. -/
  arc_endpoints (e : G.edgeSet) : Sym2.map vertex e = s(arc e 0, arc e 1)
  /-- The interior of an arc does not pass through the image of any vertex. -/
  arc_interior_not_mem_range (e : G.edgeSet) (t : I) (ht : t ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) :
    arc e t ∉ Set.range vertex

variable {G : SimpleGraph V}

/-- The crossings of a drawing: an unordered pair of distinct edges together with a point of the
plane lying in the interior of both of their arcs. -/
def Drawing.crossings (D : Drawing G) : Set (Sym2 G.edgeSet × ℝ²) :=
  {c | ∃ e f : G.edgeSet, e ≠ f ∧ c.1 = s(e, f) ∧
    c.2 ∈ D.arc e '' Set.Ioo 0 1 ∧ c.2 ∈ D.arc f '' Set.Ioo 0 1}

/-- The crossing number of a graph: the minimum number of crossings over all of its drawings in
the plane. This is `⊤` if the graph has no drawing, which cannot happen for finite graphs. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ D : Drawing G, D.crossings.encard

/-- A drawing of a graph with no edges has no crossings. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem Drawing.crossings_bot (D : Drawing (⊥ : SimpleGraph V)) : D.crossings = ∅ := by
  ext ⟨p, x⟩
  simp only [Drawing.crossings, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
  rintro ⟨⟨e, he⟩, -⟩
  simp at he

/-- A graph with no edges on a countable vertex set has crossing number zero. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem crossingNumber_bot [Countable V] : crossingNumber (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := exists_injective_nat V
  have hbot : ∀ e : (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).edgeSet, False := fun e => by simpa using e.2
  let D : Drawing (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) :=
    { vertex := fun v => EuclideanSpace.single 0 (f v : ℝ)
      vertex_injective := fun v w hvw => by
        have := congrArg (fun p : ℝ² => p 0) hvw
        simpa [EuclideanSpace.single_apply, hf.eq_iff] using this
      arc := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      arc_continuous := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      arc_injective := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      arc_endpoints := fun e => (hbot e).elim
      arc_interior_not_mem_range := fun e => (hbot e).elim }
  rw [crossingNumber, ENat.iInf_eq_zero]
  exact ⟨D, by rw [D.crossings_bot, Set.encard_empty]⟩

/-- The crossing number is monotone: a drawing of `G` restricts to a drawing of any subgraph
`H ≤ G` with no more crossings. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem crossingNumber_mono {H : SimpleGraph V} (hHG : H ≤ G) :
    crossingNumber H ≤ crossingNumber G := by
  let ι : H.edgeSet → G.edgeSet := fun e => ⟨e, SimpleGraph.edgeSet_mono hHG e.2⟩
  have hι : Function.Injective ι := fun e f h => Subtype.ext (congrArg Subtype.val h :)
  refine le_iInf fun D => ?_
  let D' : Drawing H :=
    { vertex := D.vertex
      vertex_injective := D.vertex_injective
      arc := fun e => D.arc (ι e)
      arc_continuous := fun e => D.arc_continuous (ι e)
      arc_injective := fun e => D.arc_injective (ι e)
      arc_endpoints := fun e => D.arc_endpoints (ι e)
      arc_interior_not_mem_range := fun e => D.arc_interior_not_mem_range (ι e) }
  refine (iInf_le _ D').trans ?_
  have hinj : Function.Injective (Prod.map (Sym2.map ι) (id : ℝ² → ℝ²)) :=
    (Sym2.map.injective hι).prodMap Function.injective_id
  rw [← hinj.encard_image]
  refine Set.encard_le_encard ?_
  rintro ⟨p, x⟩ ⟨⟨q, y⟩, ⟨e, f, hef, rfl, hx1, hx2⟩, h⟩
  simp only [Prod.map, id, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
  obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := h
  exact ⟨ι e, ι f, fun h => hef (hι h), by simp, hx1, hx2⟩

/--
**Albertson conjecture**

Every finite simple graph $G$ has crossing number at least that of the complete graph with the
same chromatic number: if $\chi(G) = n$, then $\operatorname{cr}(G) \ge \operatorname{cr}(K_n)$.
Equivalently, among all graphs with chromatic number $n$, the complete graph $K_n$ has the
smallest crossing number.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem albertson_conjecture [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (n : ℕ)
    (hn : G.chromaticNumber = n) :
    crossingNumber (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)) ≤ crossingNumber G := by
  sorry

end AlbertsonConjecture

items: Used the 'same chromatic number' form of the list entry (χ(G) = n → cr(K_n) ≤ cr(G)) rather than the Albertson–Cranston–Fox form (r ≤ χ(G) → cr(K_r) ≤ cr(G)); the two agree since cr(K_r) is monotone in r (a special case of the proved lemma crossingNumber_mono).

Graphs are finite ([Finite V]) simple graphs (Mathlib's SimpleGraph), as in the source; the chromatic number is Mathlib's SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber (in ℕ∞), pinned to a natural number n by the hypothesis.

A drawing (structure Drawing G) is the classical topological one: vertices mapped injectively to ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2); each edge e mapped to a Jordan arc, i.e. a continuous injective map unitInterval → ℝ², whose endpoint set {arc e 0, arc e 1} equals the image of the edge's two endpoints (orientation free, via Sym2.map), and whose interior avoids all vertex images. No 'good drawing' genericity conditions (adjacent edges don't cross, no touchings, no triple points, pairs cross at most once, finitely many intersections) are imposed; these are WLOG and do not change the minimum.

A crossing of a drawing is an unordered pair of DISTINCT edges together with a point of the plane lying in the interior images of both arcs (Set (Sym2 G.edgeSet × ℝ²)). Counting uses Set.encard (so two arcs overlapping along a segment contribute ⊤, never a spurious 0 as Set.ncard would). The number of crossings of a drawing in this convention coincides with the standard count on good drawings, and every drawing dominates some good drawing, so the infimum is the standard crossing number.

crossingNumber G : ℕ∞ := ⨅ D : Drawing G, D.crossings.encard. For finite graphs drawings exist (e.g. straight-line drawings with vertices in general position), so the value is a finite natural number and the inequality is not vacuous; the ⊤ case can only occur for graphs with no drawing at all.

Because the task restricts all writing to the candidate file, the reusable definitions Drawing/crossings/crossingNumber live in the problem file under namespace AlbertsonConjecture; in a real PR they would belong in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/CrossingNumber.lean. Two proved API lemmas (crossingNumber_bot, crossingNumber_mono) and Drawing.crossings_bot test the definitions.
Only the conjecture itself is stated: Guy's formula strengthening, the Ω(n^4) weaker form, and the n ≤ 18 special cases are not posed by the statement and are omitted, per the decomposition notes.

reviewer_notes: Source statement is a terse list entry; resolved (per the article and ACF09/BT10) as the universal finite-graph statement cr(G) ≥ cr(K_{χ(G)}), stated as χ(G) = n → cr(K_n) ≤ cr(G). The crossing number is not in Mathlib, so the file defines Drawing/crossings/crossingNumber in the problem file (a reviewer may prefer moving them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/). Faithfulness of the bespoke crossing number rests on the standard fact that the minimum over arbitrary Jordan-arc drawings, counting (edge-pair, common interior point) incidences, equals the classical crossing number: crossing-minimal drawings can be taken good (where the count is exact), and touchings, repeated meetings, adjacent-edge meetings and k-fold points only over-count (overlapping arcs give ⊤). Boundary cases: χ(G) = 0 (empty graph) gives cr(K_0) = 0 ≤ cr(G); ⊤ is unreachable for finite graphs (drawings exist; crossingNumber_bot witnesses this for ⊥). No candidate omitted the slot; the strengthened Guy-formula form and Ω(n^4) weak form were correctly excluded by all. Final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.
statement: The Albertson conjecture: the crossing number can be lower-bounded by the crossing number of a complete graph with the same chromatic number
